linear cli

 [!NOTE]
 This README is for the upcoming 4.0 release. For stable instructions, see the latest stable release (v3.1.0).

a cli to list, start and create issues in the linear issue tracker. git and jj aware to keep you in the right views in linear. allows jumping to the web or the linear desktop app similar to gh .

 works great with AI agents — the CLI includes a skill that lets agents create issues, update status, and manage your Linear workflow alongside your code. install it with linear skill setup .

see docs/authentication.md for multi-workspace support and other authentication options.

the CLI works with both git and jj version control systems:

- git : linear issue git start ABC-123 creates the branch Linear suggests for the issue and starts the issue. branch names that include the issue ID let Linear's GitHub integration link your pull requests, and @git reads the issue back from the current branch's name ( linear issue view @git ).
- jj : linear issue jj start ABC-123 starts a change (or reuses an empty, undescribed one) described with the issue title and Linear-issue trailers, or add them yourself with jj describe -m "$(linear issue describe ABC-123)" . @jj reads back every issue the trailers in trunk()..@ name ( linear issue view @jj ). to open a pull request, push a bookmark with jj first and name it with --head (see below)

each command names its tool ( issue git … , issue jj … , issue gh … ), and nothing is chosen by a setting: linear issue gh pr builds the title and body and runs gh pr create ; linear itself never creates, moves or pushes a branch or bookmark. the vcs setting ( LINEAR VCS ) was removed in 4.0; old values are ignored quietly and are safe to leave in place. pr template ( LINEAR PR TEMPLATE ), the old starting-body file setting, was removed too: pass description text with linear issue gh pr --body-file . An old setting is reported only when creating a pull request or running linear config check ; it is safe to keep. use new MiniJinja preferences to configure generated guide, commit and PR layouts

 commands

 issue commands

every command takes the issue it acts on: an ID like ENG-123 , an issue URL, a bare number in the configured team, or a reference that reads it from your repository. @git is the first issue ID in the current git branch's name; @jj is every issue named by the Linear-issue trailers of the changes in trunk()..@ . the cli reads the repository only when you pass one of these, and says on stderr which issues it read before anything is sent. a command that acts on one issue refuses a reference that names several; issue view and the pull request commands take them all. in PowerShell, quote them: '@git' .

 

 pull requests

 issue gh pr fetches the issues, builds the title and body, and runs gh pr create . before -- is what linear builds; everything after -- goes to gh unchanged, after linear's --title and --body , so a flag there wins (a --title or --body after -- replaces linear's, issue links included; gh's own --template cannot be used, since linear always passes a body). the shipped title is ABC-123 for one issue, and several issues require --title . template preferences can generate a multiissue title and customize the complete body; an explicit --title always wins. --body or --body-file supplies description data to the body template, whose shipped layout appends Fixes ABC-123 (or References … with --references ) and each issue URL. linear itself never pushes: without -- --head , gh opens the pull request from the current git branch and, in a terminal, may offer to push it (or fork the repository) first; -- --head names a branch that is already pushed and turns that off. from jj, push the bookmark first, then pass it with -- --head . @- assumes @ is an empty scratch change on top of the finished one; right after issue jj start , @ is the described change, so run jj new first (or push @ ):

 

later, jj git push --bookmark "$branch" updates the pull request. the bookmark follows a rewritten change on its own; after adding new commits on top, first run jj bookmark move "$branch" --to @- .

 attaching files

attach files to an issue or comment. uploads are private by default (readable only by workspace members), matching the Linear web app.

 

by default attachments are private. pass --public to upload raster images (png/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/tiff) to a public public.linear.app URL readable by anyone, unauthenticated — useful for sharing outside the workspace, but a warning is printed since it bypasses workspace access controls. non-image files cannot be made public.

manage Linear documents from the command line. every document is attached to exactly one target: a project, issue, initiative, team, cycle, or release (Linear's API requires one).

intro.html:
[!NOTE] This README is for the upcoming 4.0 release. For stable instructions, see the latest stable release (v3.1.0).

a cli to list, start and create issues in the linear issue tracker. git and jj aware to keep you in the right views in linear. allows jumping to the web or the linear desktop app similar to gh.

works great with AI agents — the CLI includes a skill that lets agents create issues, update status, and manage your Linear workflow alongside your code. install it with linear skill setup.

here's how it works:

linear config               # setup your repo, it writes a config file

linear issue mine           # list unstarted issues assigned to you
linear issue query --all-teams  # query issues across all teams
linear issue query --search "login bug"  # search issues in your configured team
linear issue start ABC-123  # move an issue to its team's first started status
linear issue git start      # choose an issue, create its branch, and start it
linear issue view ABC-123   # see an issue as markdown
linear issue gh pr ABC-123  # makes a PR with title/body preset, using gh cli
linear issue create         # create a new issue

it aims to be a complement to the web and desktop apps that lets you stay on the command line in an interactive or scripted way.

install.title: install
install.html:
homebrew
brew install schpet/tap/linear
npm / bun / pnpm

install as a dev dependency to pin a version in your project:

npm install -D @schpet/linear-cli
# or
bun add -D @schpet/linear-cli
# or
pnpm add -D @schpet/linear-cli

then run via your package manager:

npx linear issue mine
bunx linear issue mine

note: this package ships pre-built binaries

package on npm: @schpet/linear-cli

shell installer

for macOS and Linux:

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/schpet/linear-cli/releases/latest/download/linear-installer.sh | sh
binaries

https://github.com/schpet/linear-cli/releases/latest

from source

with a rust toolchain installed:

cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/schpet/linear-cli linear
nix

run it without installing, with flakes enabled:

nix run github:schpet/linear-cli -- --version

or install it into your profile:

nix profile install github:schpet/linear-cli

the flake builds from source on linux and apple silicon macOS. as a flake input it provides packages.<system>.linear and overlays.default, which adds pkgs.linear.

upgrading from 2.x? see upgrading from 2.x in the changelog.

usage.title: commands
usage.html:
issue commands

every command takes the issue it acts on: an ID like ENG-123, an issue URL, a bare number in the configured team, or a reference that reads it from your repository. @git is the first issue ID in the current git branch's name; @jj is every issue named by the Linear-issue trailers of the changes in trunk()..@. the cli reads the repository only when you pass one of these, and says on stderr which issues it read before anything is sent. a command that acts on one issue refuses a reference that names several; issue view and the pull request commands take them all. in PowerShell, quote them: '@git'.

linear issue view ABC-123  # view issue details in terminal
linear issue view 123
linear issue view ABC-123 ABC-124         # multiple issues, in argument order
linear issue view ABC-123 ABC-124 --json  # an array; one issue returns an object
linear issue view ABC-123 -w   # open issue in web browser
linear issue view ABC-123 -a   # open issue in Linear.app
linear issue title ABC-123     # prints just the issue title
linear issue url ABC-123       # prints the Linear.app URL for the issue
linear issue gh pr ABC-123     # creates a GitHub PR with issue details via `gh pr create`
linear issue gh pr @git        # the same, for the issue in the current git branch's name
linear issue gh pr ABC-123 ABC-124 --title "Fix login"  # one PR for several issues: "Fixes ABC-123 and ABC-124" and their URLs in the body
linear issue gh pr ABC-123 -F body.md  # your description, then the issue links
linear issue gh pr ABC-123 -- --draft --base main  # everything after -- goes to `gh pr create`
linear issue gh pr @jj --title "Fix login" -- --head my-topic  # one PR for every issue the trailers in trunk()..@ name, from a pushed branch
linear issue id @jj            # prints the issues @jj reads, one per line
linear issue mine      # list your issues in a table view (supports -s/--state and --sort)
linear issue mine --project "My Project" --milestone "Phase 1"  # filter by milestone
linear issue mine -w   # open your issues in the web browser
linear issue mine -a   # open your issues in Linear.app
linear issue query --search "login bug"  # search issues by text in your configured team
linear issue query --search "oauth timeout" --team ENG --json  # structured search output for agents
linear issue query --team "Engineering" --state "In Review" --json  # teams by key, name, or ID; states by type, name, or ID
linear issue query --all-teams --json --limit all  # export all issues as JSON
linear issue start ENG-123     # move the issue to its team's first started status; touches nothing in your repo
linear issue complete ENG-123  # move the issue to its team's completed status
linear issue cancel ENG-123    # move the issue to its team's canceled status
linear issue git start ENG-123 # create/switch to the issue's git branch, then start it (--branch, --from-ref); prints what it did
linear issue jj start ENG-123  # start a jj change described with the issue, then start it; prints the change ID, description and trailers it wrote
linear issue create    # create a new issue, asking for the title
linear issue create -i # create a new issue, asking for every field
linear issue create -t "title" -d "description"  # create with flags
linear issue create --project "My Project" --milestone "Phase 1"  # create with milestone
linear issue create --template "Bug report" -t "Login fails"  # create from a template (see template commands)
linear issue update ENG-123 -s started  # change only the fields you pass
linear issue update ENG-123 --milestone "Phase 2"  # set milestone on existing issue
linear issue update ENG-123 --clear-due-date --clear-parent  # remove values (also --clear-estimate, --clear-project, --clear-milestone, --clear-cycle, --unassign)
linear issue archive ENG-123 --yes  # archive an issue (Linear normally auto-archives closed issues; see docs/usage.md)
linear issue archive --yes --bulk ENG-123 ENG-124  # archive several issues
linear issue delete ENG-123   # delete an issue
linear issue comment list ENG-123          # list comments on an issue
linear issue comment add ENG-123           # add a comment to an issue
linear issue comment add ENG-123 --reply-to <id>   # reply to a comment (-p / --parent are aliases)
linear issue comment list ENG-123 --json   # comments as JSON, with quotedText and parent for inline comments and replies
linear issue comment update <id>   # update a comment
pull requests

issue gh pr fetches the issues, builds the title and body, and runs gh pr create. before -- is what linear builds; everything after -- goes to gh unchanged, after linear's --title and --body, so a flag there wins (a --title or --body after -- replaces linear's, issue links included; gh's own --template cannot be used, since linear always passes a body). the shipped title is ABC-123 <issue title> for one issue, and several issues require --title. template preferences can generate a multiissue title and customize the complete body; an explicit --title always wins. --body or --body-file supplies description data to the body template, whose shipped layout appends Fixes ABC-123 (or References … with --references) and each issue URL. linear itself never pushes: without -- --head, gh opens the pull request from the current git branch and, in a terminal, may offer to push it (or fork the repository) first; -- --head <branch> names a branch that is already pushed and turns that off. from jj, push the bookmark first, then pass it with -- --head. @- assumes @ is an empty scratch change on top of the finished one; right after issue jj start, @ is the described change, so run jj new first (or push @):

branch=$(linear issue view ABC-123 --json | jq -r .branchName)
jj git push --named "$branch=@-"             # first push: creates the bookmark
linear issue gh pr ABC-123 -- --head "$branch"  # add --repo OWNER/REPO after -- in a non-colocated jj repository

later, jj git push --bookmark "$branch" updates the pull request. the bookmark follows a rewritten change on its own; after adding new commits on top, first run jj bookmark move "$branch" --to @-.

attaching files

attach files to an issue or comment. uploads are private by default (readable only by workspace members), matching the Linear web app.

linear issue attach ENG-123 ./screenshot.png            # attach a file to an issue
linear issue attach ENG-123 ./doc.pdf -t "Spec"         # custom attachment title
linear issue attach ENG-123 ./img.png -c "see this"     # add a linked comment
linear issue comment add ENG-123 -a ./screenshot.png    # attach a file to a comment
linear issue comment add ENG-123 -a ./a.png -a ./b.png  # attach multiple files

by default attachments are private. pass --public to upload raster images (png/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/tiff) to a public public.linear.app URL readable by anyone, unauthenticated — useful for sharing outside the workspace, but a warning is printed since it bypasses workspace access controls. non-image files cannot be made public.

linear issue attach ENG-123 ./screenshot.png --public           # public image URL
linear issue comment add ENG-123 -a ./screenshot.png --public   # public image URL
team commands
linear team list       # list teams
linear team list --json  # as JSON, e.g. to map a team name to its key or id in scripts
linear team id         # print the configured team key (e.g. for scripts)
linear team members    # list team members
linear team members --all --json  # include inactive members, as JSON
linear team create     # create a new team
linear team autolinks  # configure GitHub repository autolinks for Linear issues
user commands
linear user list        # list everyone in the workspace
linear user list --all  # include deactivated members
linear user list --json # machine-readable output
project commands
